subject.title: feat(slack): Support Slack RTS (Real-Time Search) API via assistant action tokens

question: Should OpenClaw add Slack RTS as a bundled Slack-plugin `assistant.search.context` action, and what token/privacy/scope contract should govern event-scoped Slack `action_token`s?
rationale: The requested behavior adds workspace-wide Slack search and ephemeral action-token handling, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent API shape, retention model, or privacy boundary.

options.title: Add narrow RTS support
options.body: Implement a Slack-owned read-only RTS action with ephemeral, redacted, thread/account-bound action tokens and live Slack validation.

options.title: Defer to external plugin
options.body: Leave the bundled Slack plugin unchanged until maintainers want OpenClaw to own the RTS security and scope contract.

options.title: Use legacy user-token search instead
options.body: Pursue `search.messages`-style user-token search, accepting that it is not the requested event-token RTS API and needs a separate product/security review.

recommendation.title: Add narrow RTS support
recommendation.body: Implement a Slack-owned read-only RTS action with ephemeral, redacted, thread/account-bound action tokens and live Slack validation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest Slack assistant lifecycle and action-surface history around the affected files and related closed PRs.
